issues.detail: Error handling is covered only for model load failures; it omits GPU out-of-memory, request timeouts, shape or datatype mismatches at inference time, and client-side retry behavior.

scenarios.name: serve-torchscript-model-cpu
scenarios.rationale: Both cover layout, KIND_CPU, dims excluding the batch dimension, no --gpus, and readiness checks. B states that TorchScript needs a config because Triton can't auto-generate one, which the rubric asks for, and pins a concrete tag (26.09-py3). A leaves the tag as the placeholder <yy.mm> and only implies that a config is needed, though it adds useful extras.

scenarios.name: tokenizer-classifier-ensemble
scenarios.rationale: B covers more of the rubric: it has the ensemble config with correct input_map/output_map and an empty version dir, and it includes a Python backend model config plus the model.py tokenizer snippet, but not a full TritonPythonModel class. A has the ensemble config and empty version dir but includes no Python backend model or TritonPythonModel class at all.

scenarios.name: tune-batching-and-fix-unavailable-model
scenarios.rationale: A covers the curl config check, dynamic_batching with max_queue_delay_microseconds, instance_group count 2/KIND_GPU/gpus [0], positive max_batch_size, Perf Analyzer, and explicitly avoids preferred_batch_size for non-TensorRT models, while B uses preferred_batch_size on an ONNX model (contrary to the rubric), relies on an onnx script and the deprecated strict-model-config flag as the primary diagnosis, and never mentions the startup status table, though it does include the curl command and perf_analyzer.
